# SEC-08 (#796): CI supply-chain gate. Runs on EVERY PR — no path gating,
  # a security gate you can dodge with a cunning diff is not a gate.
  supply-chain:
    name: Supply-chain gate
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: changes
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # Known limit: pull_request/dispatched runs execute THIS file and the
      # checker from the PR's own head — a PR can edit the gate in the same
      # diff. Backstops: reviewers see workflow edits, Dependabot PRs
      # re-verify on main, and the gate is re-enforced by any post-merge
      # scheduled run. A hard guarantee needs a separate workflow_call gate
      # pinned by SHA, invoked from a caller that never comes from the PR
      # (follow-up issue, not this PR).

      # AC1: zero mutable third-party action refs (script + CI job).
      - name: AC1 — all third-party actions SHA-pinned
        run: bash scripts/check_action_pins.sh

      # AC2: every workflow declares an explicit top-level permissions block.
      - name: AC2 — every workflow declares top-level permissions
        run: |
          status=0
          shopt -s nullglob
          for f in .github/workflows/*.yml .github/workflows/*.yaml; do
            [ -f "$f" ] || continue
            if ! grep -q '^permissions:' "$f"; then
              echo "::error file=$f::missing top-level permissions: block"
              status=1
            fi
          done
          exit $status

      # AC4 (REG): the checker must reject a @v4 fixture, a 40-char NON-hex
      # ref (mutable branch with a SHA-shaped name), and a nested composite
      # action manifest — and accept clean equivalents. A gate that cannot
      # fail is decoration.
      - name: AC4 — pin-checker fixture regression
        run: |
          tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
          trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT
          mkdir -p "$tmp/bad" "$tmp/bad-hex" "$tmp/bad-composite/.github/actions/probe/deep" "$tmp/good" "$tmp/good-composite/.github/actions/probe/deep" "$tmp/string-safe"
          printf 'jobs:\n  probe:\n    steps:\n      - uses: actions/checkout@v4\n' > "$tmp/bad/bad.yml"
          printf 'jobs:\n  probe:\n    steps:\n      - uses: actions/checkout@gggggggggggggggggggggggggggggggggggggggg\n' > "$tmp/bad-hex/bad.yml"
          printf 'name: probe\nruns:\n  using: composite\n  steps:\n    - uses: actions/checkout@v4\n' > "$tmp/bad-composite/.github/actions/probe/deep/action.yaml"
          printf 'jobs:\n  probe:\n    steps:\n      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v4\n' > "$tmp/good/good.yml"
          printf 'name: probe\nruns:\n  using: composite\n  steps:\n    - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v4\n' > "$tmp/good-composite/.github/actions/probe/deep/action.yaml"
          # String-safety: a uses-shaped string INSIDE a run: scalar is not a
          # step ref — the checker is line-anchored (^[[:space:]]*(- )?uses:)
          # and must not flag it. (Regression: a reviewer suspected the
          # fixture printf lines in this very workflow would trip AC1.)
          printf "jobs:\n  probe:\n    steps:\n      - name: write fixture\n        run: |\n          printf 'jobs:\\\\n  probe:\\\\n    steps:\\\\n      - uses: actions/checkout@v4\\\\n' > out.yml\n          bash scripts/check_action_pins.sh --path . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true\n" > "$tmp/string-safe/wf.yml"
          for bad in bad bad-hex bad-composite; do
            if bash scripts/check_action_pins.sh --path "$tmp/$bad" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              echo "::error::pin checker FAILED to flag the $bad fixture"
              exit 1
            fi
          done
          bash scripts/check_action_pins.sh --path "$tmp/good" >/dev/null
          bash scripts/check_action_pins.sh --path "$tmp/good-composite" >/dev/null
          bash scripts/check_action_pins.sh --path "$tmp/string-safe" >/dev/null
          echo "fixture regression OK: @v4 / 40-char non-hex / unpinned nested composite rejected; SHA-pinned accepted; uses-shaped run-scalar strings ignored"

  # SEC-08 (#796): audit BOTH dependency graphs. pubspec_overrides.yaml
  # redirects dart_tui to the vendored fork (vendor/dart_tui) for local/CI/
  # release builds while pubspec.yaml pins hosted dart_tui for the published
  # package — two different graphs; an audit of one says nothing about the
  # other. Each graph gets its own matrix leg and the split is documented in
  # the audit output.
  dep-audit:
    name: Dependency audit (${{ matrix.graph }})
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: changes
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        graph: [hosted, vendored]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      # Hosted leg = exactly what pub.dev consumers resolve; the overrides
      # file never ships, so it must not bend this graph.
      - name: Park vendored overrides (hosted leg)
        if: matrix.graph == 'hosted'
        run: |
          [ -f pubspec_overrides.yaml ] || {
            echo "::error::pubspec_overrides.yaml missing — hosted-leg precondition broke, parking nothing would bend the graph silently"
            exit 1
          }
          mv pubspec_overrides.yaml pubspec_overrides.yaml.vendored
      - run: dart pub get
      - name: Audit the ${{ matrix.graph }} dependency graph
        env:
          GRAPH: ${{ matrix.graph }}
        run: |
          {
            echo "### Dependency audit — \`${GRAPH}\` graph"
            echo ""
            echo "This repo resolves TWO dependency graphs (SEC-08):"
            echo "- **hosted** — \`pubspec.yaml\` alone: what \`pub publish\` ships and pub.dev consumers resolve (dart_tui hosted)."
            echo "- **vendored** — \`pubspec.yaml\` + \`pubspec_overrides.yaml\`: local dev, CI and the release binaries (dart_tui rides \`vendor/dart_tui\`)."
            echo ""
            echo "An audit of one says nothing about the other, so both are audited on every run. Resolved graph:"
            echo ""
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          dart pub deps --style=compact | tee /tmp/graph.txt >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY" || true
          {
            echo ""
            echo "Outdated direct dependencies (informational):"
            echo '```'
            dart pub outdated
            echo '```'
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY" || true
          # The split must be REAL: each leg resolves dart_tui from its own
          # source, read from the resolved pubspec.lock. The block runs from
          # the `dart_tui:` entry header to the next top-level entry header
          # (two-space indent) — no fixed line window to rot.
          lock_block=$(awk 'f && /^  [A-Za-z0-9_.-]+:$/ { exit } /^  dart_tui:$/ { f = 1 } f { print }' pubspec.lock)
          # Vacuous-assertion guard: if dart_tui ever leaves the lock (or
          # the entry is renamed) the block is empty and the per-graph
          # greps below would fail bare (exit 1, no annotation) or — worse
          # for future shape changes — pass on nothing. Fail loudly here.
          [ -n "$lock_block" ] || {
            echo "::error::no dart_tui entry found in pubspec.lock — the audit assertion is vacuous, aborting"
            exit 1
          }
          echo "$lock_block"
          case "$GRAPH" in
            hosted)
              if echo "$lock_block" | grep -q 'source: path'; then
                echo "::error::hosted graph resolved the vendored dart_tui fork"
                exit 1

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# check_action_pins.sh — SEC-08 (#796) AC1/AC4: mutable references to
# executable code are lint errors. Fails on any third-party GitHub Actions
# `uses:` ref that is not pinned to…

blocks.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# check_action_pins.sh — SEC-08 (#796) AC1/AC4: mutable references to
# executable code are lint errors. Fails on any third-party GitHub Actions
# `uses:` ref that is not pinned to a full commit SHA.
#
#   bash scripts/check_action_pins.sh            # scan the repo (CI gate)
#   bash scripts/check_action_pins.sh --path DIR # scan DIR/*.yml (fixtures)
#
# Exempt:
#   - ./...          first-party repo-relative actions/workflows
#   - @<40-hex>      full commit SHA (the only accepted third-party form)
# Everything else (tags, branches, latest, main, master, short SHAs) fails.

set -eu

dir=".github/workflows"
if [ "${1:-}" = "--path" ]; then
  [ -n "${2:-}" ] || { echo "usage: $0 [--path DIR]" >&2; exit 2; }
  dir="$2"
fi

shopt -s nullglob
# Both modes share one shape: the root's workflows (either a
# .github/workflows layout or loose *.yml/*.yaml fixtures) plus EVERY
# composite action manifest at any depth — composite action steps can
# carry remote uses: refs, so they are part of AC1's threat surface.
files=("$dir"/.github/workflows/*.yml "$dir"/.github/workflows/*.yaml \
       "$dir"/*.yml "$dir"/*.yaml)
# Default (CI) mode: composite actions live under .github/actions/, OUTSIDE
# the workflows dir — root the manifest sweep at the repo root so they
# are covered (a regression here would let an unpinned remote uses: sail
# through AC1). Prune .worktrees: sibling checkouts are not this repo's
# gate surface. Fixture mode (--path) stays rooted at DIR: fixtures are
# self-contained trees.
root="$dir"
if [ "$dir" = ".github/workflows" ] && [ -d "$dir" ]; then
  root="."
fi
while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
  files+=("$f")
done < <(find "$root" -name .git -prune -o -path './.worktrees' -prune -o -type f \( -name 'action.yml' -o -name 'action.yaml' \) -print0 2>/dev/null)

if [ ${#files[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "no workflow files found under $dir" >&2
  exit 2
fi

violations=0
for file in "${files[@]}"; do
  refs=$(grep -hoE '^[[:space:]]*(-[[:space:]]+)?uses:[[:space:]]*[^[:space:]]+' "$file" 2>/dev/null | sed -E 's/.*uses:[[:space:]]*//') || true
  [ -n "$refs" ] || continue
  while IFS= read -r ref; do
    [ -n "$ref" ] || continue
    case "$ref" in
      ./*) ;; # first-party repo-relative action/workflow
      docker://*)
        case "$ref" in
          *@sha256:*) ;; # digest-pinned container image
          *)
            echo "::error file=$file::unpinned container image ref: $ref"
            violations=$((violations + 1))
            ;;
        esac
        ;;
      *)
        sha="${ref##*@}"
        # A mutable ref whose NAME is exactly 40 chars would pass a pure
        # length glob — require hex digits (a commit SHA), nothing else.
        if [[ "$sha" =~ ^[0-9a-fA-F]{40}$ ]]; then
          : # full 40-hex commit SHA — the only accepted third-party form
        else
          echo "::error file=$file::third-party action not SHA-pinned: $ref"
          violations=$((violations + 1))
        fi
        ;;
    esac
  done <<EOF
$refs
EOF
done

if [ "$violations" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo "check_action_pins: $violations mutable third-party action ref(s)" >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "check_action_pins: OK (all third-party actions SHA-pinned)"

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger …

Owner directive 2026-10-04: consumers follow awf main instead of immutable SHA pins — fixes (kicker real ticks awf#13, per-SHA concurrency awf#14, teammate defaults awf#12) go live on merge, no re-pin ceremony per consumer.

Security trade-off (accepted by owner): a mutable ref executes whatever sits at awf main head. Supersedes the original fd84ab19 re-pin description (pre-directive plan).

blocks.text:
# Factory Merge Trigger — the canonical pr_approved merge bot.
#
# One reusable implementation for every factory repo. The calling repo
# keeps a thin stub that declares the EVENT triggers (workflow_run on its
# CI workflow, optionally issues:labeled) and calls this one — `on:` in a
# stub cannot be parameterized, everything below the event boundary is
# shared here.
#
# The tracker is the CALLING repo's GitHub issues (no Jira, no external
# services):
#
#   issue labeled `pr_approved` → linked PR found → required checks green
#   (branch protection is the gate: mergeStateStatus CLEAN) → squash-merge
#   → label removed → comment posted on the issue.
#
# Linking conventions (any of):
#   - PR body contains `Closes #NN` / `Fixes #NN` / `Resolves #NN`
#   - PR branch name starts with `NN-` (e.g. `42-fix-foo`)
#   - PR branch name matches `gh-0*NN` (the gh-N display-title convention)
#   - the PR itself carries the label (pr_review approves via
#     scm.addLabel) — mapped back to its linked issue
#
# Prerequisites (in the calling repo):
#   vars: MERGE_TRIGGER_ENABLED (fuse — the job skips itself until `true`)
#   branch protection on main with required checks + strict (the machine
#   only merges CLEAN PRs, so protection defines what "ready" means).
#   github.token is sufficient for everything; pass a PAT via
#   secrets: inherit if the caller needs one (see GH_TOKEN below).

name: Factory Merge Trigger

run-name: 'Merge Trigger : CI passed → merge pr_approved issues'

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      runner:
        description: 'Runs-on label for the merge job'
        type: string
        default: 'ubuntu-latest'
      remove_pr_label:
        description: 'Also remove pr_approved from the merged PR (dmd convention)'
        type: boolean
        default: true
      map_pr_labels:
        description: 'Map PRs labeled pr_approved back to their linked issues'
        type: boolean
        default: true
      gh_branch_pattern:
        description: 'Also link via branch names like gh-0*NN'
        type: boolean
        default: true

permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write
  actions: read

jobs:
  merge-trigger:
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner }}
    timeout-minutes: 10
    # Same-repo guard: PRs from forks must not trigger merges. The
    # issues:labeled entry path (dmd) re-enters without a workflow_run.
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'issues' && github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved') ||
      (github.event_name == 'workflow_run' &&
       github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success' &&
       github.event.workflow_run.head_repository.full_name == github.repository)
    concurrency:
      group: merge-trigger-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha || github.event.issue.number }}
      cancel-in-progress: false
    steps:
      - name: Gate on MERGE_TRIGGER_ENABLED
        id: gate
        env:
          ENABLED: ${{ vars.MERGE_TRIGGER_ENABLED }}
        run: |
          if [ "$ENABLED" = "true" ]; then
            echo "enabled=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "enabled=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::merge-trigger scaffold is wired but disabled — set the MERGE_TRIGGER_ENABLED repo variable to true (after branch protection + required checks are in place)."
          fi

      - name: Merge issues labeled pr_approved
        if: steps.gate.outputs.enabled == 'true'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.PAT_TOKEN || github.token }}
          LABEL: pr_approved
          CI_RUN_URL: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.html_url }}
          REMOVE_PR_LABEL: ${{ inputs.remove_pr_label }}
          MAP_PR_LABELS: ${{ inputs.map_pr_labels }}
          GH_BRANCH_PATTERN: ${{ inputs.gh_branch_pattern }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          repo="${{ github.repository }}"
          # Candidates come from BOTH sides: the issue label (human/bot)
          # and the PR label (pr_review approves via scm.addLabel on the
          # PR) — map PR labels back to their linked issues.
          issues=$(gh issue list --repo "$repo" --label "$LABEL" --state open \
            --json number --jq '.[].number')
          if [ "$MAP_PR_LABELS" = "true" ]; then
            prs_labeled=$(gh pr list --repo "$repo" --label "$LABEL" --state open \
              --json number,body,headRefName --jq '.[] | "\(.number)\t\(.body // "")\t\(.headRefName)"')
            while IFS=$'\t' read -r prn body branch; do
              [ -n "$prn" ] || continue
              n=$(echo "$body" | grep -oiE '\b(closes|fixes|resolves)\s+#[0-9]+' | head -1 | grep -oE '[0-9]+' || true)
              [ -n "$n" ] || n=$(echo "$branch" | grep -oE '^[0-9]+' || true)
              [ -n "$n" ] || n=$(echo "$branch" | grep -oE 'gh-[0-9]+' | head -1 | grep -oE '[0-9]+' || true)
              if [ -n "$n" ]; then
                open=$(gh issue view "$n" --repo "$repo" --json state --jq .state 2>/dev/null || true)
                [ "$open" = "OPEN" ] && issues="$issues $n"
              fi
            done < <(printf '%s\n' "$prs_labeled")
            issues=$(echo $issues | tr ' ' '\n' | sort -u | tr '\n' ' ')
          fi
          if [ -z "${issues// /}" ]; then
            echo "no issues labeled '$LABEL' — nothing to merge"
            exit 0
          fi
          merged=0; skipped=0
          for n in $issues; do
            echo "::group::issue #$n"
            gh_pat='(?i)\\b(closes|fixes|resolves)\\s+#'"$n"'\\b'
            branch_pat='^'"$n"'[-_.]'
            if [ "$GH_BRANCH_PATTERN" = "true" ]; then
              link_sel="((.body // \"\") | test(\"$gh_pat\")) or (.headRefName | test(\"$branch_pat\")) or (.headRefName | test(\"(^|[-_./])gh-0*$n$\"))"
            else
              link_sel="((.body // \"\") | test(\"$gh_pat\")) or (.headRefName | test(\"$branch_pat\"))"
            fi
            pr=$(gh pr list --repo "$repo" --state open \
              --json number,body,headRefName \
              --jq "[.[] | select($link_sel) | .number] | first // empty")
            if [ -z "$pr" ]; then
              echo "issue #$n: no linked open PR (add 'Closes #$n' to the PR body or name the branch '$n-…') — skipping"
              skipped=$((skipped+1)); echo "::endgroup::"; continue
            fi
            state=$(gh pr view "$pr" --repo "$repo" \
              --json mergeable,mergeStateStatus \
              --jq '.mergeable + ":" + .mergeStateStatus')
            echo "linked PR #$pr — $state"
            case "$state" in
              MERGEABLE:CLEAN)
                if err=$(gh pr merge "$pr" --repo "$repo" --squash 2>&1); then
                  merged=$((merged+1))
                  gh issue edit "$n" --repo "$repo" --remove-label "$LABEL" || true
                  if [ "$REMOVE_PR_LABEL" = "true" ]; then
                    gh pr edit "$pr" --repo "$repo" --remove-label "$LABEL" || true
                  fi
                  gh issue comment "$n" --repo "$repo" \
                    --body "🔀 Merged #$pr (CI: ${CI_RUN_URL:-run})" || true
                  echo "✅ merged #$pr for issue #$n"
                else
                  skipped=$((skipped+1))
                  echo "❌ merge of #$pr failed: $err"
                fi
                ;;
              MERGEABLE:BEHIND)
                skipped=$((skipped+1)); echo "⏳ behind main — the SM (silent-update-behind) refreshes it, then re-dispatches CI"
                ;;
              MERGEABLE:BLOCKED|MERGEABLE:UNSTABLE)
                skipped=$((skipped+1)); echo "⏳ required checks not green yet"
                ;;
              *)
                skipped=$((skipped+1)); echo "⛔ not mergeable ($state) — needs manual attention"
                ;;
            esac
            echo "::endgroup::"
          done
          echo "summary: merged=$merged skipped=$skipped"

# SM kicker — a tiny watchdog (two jobs, seconds each, ~zero runner cost).
#
# Canonical home for the SM-kicker watchdog every factory repo points at.
# The calling repo keeps a thin stub workflow that calls this one with the
# repo-specific names (defaults match flutter_agent_harness).
#
# Why it exists: a repo whose CI is dispatch-only (no `on.push` on PR
# heads) and whose Machine SM is the sole trigger has two gaps that leave
# a PR BLOCKED forever with zero required-check contexts on its head:
#
#   1. SM dead: the cron tick missed/failed and nothing re-arms it.
#      Fix: if no SM run is queued/running/in-progress — dispatch one tick.
#
#   2. Head completeness: pushes WITHOUT code changes (pure main-merge
#      commits — the SM's own silent update-branch, or a manual
#      "merge main into branch") fire no workflows by design, yet strict
#      `up-to-date` protection demands FRESH required checks on the new
#      head SHA. Fix: if a PR head is a codeless merge commit (2 parents,
#      0 files vs first parent) and carries NEITHER of the required check
#      contexts NOR an active CI run — dispatch the CI workflow on it.
#
# Code-bearing pushes (dev/rework/WIP) are deliberately NOT touched here:

# Machine merge bot stub — event-driven fast path (factory pack).
#
# The SM cron tick is best-effort (GitHub silently drops scheduled runs);
# this workflow reacts to EVENTS: CI conclusion, label changes, head
# pushes, check-run completions — and runs the deterministic mergeBot
# (factory-merge.yml) so approved green PRs merge within seconds.
# Idempotent against the SM: shared labels, first actor wins.
name: 'Machine Merge Bot'

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ['CI', 'Quality']   # per-repo: fa's dispatched CI is named 'CI'
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
    types: [labeled, synchronize, edited]
  check_run:
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch: {}

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write

concurrency:
  group: machine-merge-bot
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  merge:
    # Label events only matter for the machine latches; other PR events
    # (synchronize/edited) always run — cheap and idempotent.
    if: >-
      github.event_name != 'pull_request' ||
      github.event.action != 'labeled' ||
      contains(github.event.label.name, 'ai_') ||
      contains(github.event.label.name, 'pr_approved')
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-merge.yml@main
    with:
      ci_workflow: ci.yml
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}

  those heads. Workaround until the upstream fix: keep the branch head
  code-bearing. Live instance: run 37193754301 on head 1fe9b1232.

  silently at the agent-chatter wake cap. The idle inbox-wake gate
  (`InboxWakePolicy`, shared by the CLI and the app hosts) now exempts a
  delivered scheduled self-reminder (`[scheduled] ` prefix, from == to)
  from the 10-consecutive-wake streak: a deliberate agent-chosen cadence
  (night watch, periodic sweep) wakes forever, while foreign

  mail always wakes. A 30s cadence floor bounds a zero-delay

# SEC-08 (#796): CI supply-chain gate. Runs on EVERY PR — no path gating,
  # a security gate you can dodge with a cunning diff is not a gate.
  supply-chain:
    name: Supply-chain gate
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: changes
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # Known limit: pull_request/dispatched runs execute THIS file and the
      # checker from the PR's own head — a PR can edit the gate in the same
      # diff. Backstops: reviewers see workflow edits, Dependabot PRs
      # re-verify on main, and the gate is re-enforced by any post-merge
      # scheduled run. A hard guarantee needs a separate workflow_call gate
      # pinned by SHA, invoked from a caller that never comes from the PR
      # (follow-up issue, not this PR).

      # AC1: zero mutable third-party action refs (script + CI job).
      - name: AC1 — all third-party actions SHA-pinned
        run: bash scripts/check_action_pins.sh

      # AC2: every workflow declares an explicit top-level permissions block.
      - name: AC2 — every workflow declares top-level permissions
        run: |
          status=0
          shopt -s nullglob
          for f in .github/workflows/*.yml .github/workflows/*.yaml; do

              status=1
            fi

      # ref (mutable branch with a SHA-shaped name), and a nested composite
      # action manifest — and accept clean equivalents. A gate that cannot
      # fail is decoration.
      - name: AC4 — pin-checker fixture regression
        run: |
          tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
          trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT
          mkdir -p "$tmp/bad" "$tmp/bad-hex" "$tmp/bad-composite/.github/actions/probe/deep" "$tmp/good" "$tmp/good-composite/.github/actions/probe/deep" "$tmp/string-safe"
          printf 'jobs:\n  probe:\n    steps:\n      - uses: actions/checkout@v4\n' > "$tmp/bad/bad.yml"
          printf 'jobs:\n  probe:\n    steps:\n      - uses: actions/checkout@gggggggggggggggggggggggggggggggggggggggg\n' > "$tmp/bad-hex/bad.yml"
          printf 'name: probe\nruns:\n  using: composite\n  steps:\n    - uses: actions/checkout@v4\n' > "$tmp/bad-composite/.github/actions/probe/deep/action.yaml"
          printf 'jobs:\n  probe:\n    steps:\n      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v4\n' > "$tmp/good/good.yml"
          printf 'name: probe\nruns:\n  using: composite\n  steps:\n    - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v4\n' > "$tmp/good-composite/.github/actions/probe/deep/action.yaml"
          # String-safety: a uses-shaped string INSIDE a run: scalar is not a
          # step ref — the checker is line-anchored (^[[:space:]]*(- )?uses:)
          # and must not flag it. (Regression: a reviewer suspected the
          # fixture printf lines in this very workflow would trip AC1.)
          printf "jobs:\n  probe:\n    steps:\n      - name: write fixture\n        run: |\n          printf 'jobs:\\\\n  probe:\\\\n    steps:\\\\n      - uses: actions/checkout@v4\\\\n' > out.yml\n          bash scripts/check_action_pins.sh --path . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true\n" > "$tmp/string-safe/wf.yml"
          for bad in bad bad-hex bad-composite; do
            if bash scripts/check_action_pins.sh --path "$tmp/$bad" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              echo "::error::pin checker FAILED to flag the $bad fixture"
              exit 1
            fi
          done
          bash scripts/check_action_pins.sh --path "$tmp/good" >/dev/null
          bash scripts/check_action_pins.sh --path "$tmp/good-composite" >/dev/null
          bash scripts/check_action_pins.sh --path "$tmp/string-safe" >/dev/null
          echo "fixture regression OK: @v4 / 40-char non-hex / unpinned nested composite rejected; SHA-pinned accepted; uses-shaped run-scalar strings ignored"

  # SEC-08 (#796): audit BOTH dependency graphs. pubspec_overrides.yaml
  # redirects dart_tui to the vendored fork (vendor/dart_tui) for local/CI/
  # release builds while pubspec.yaml pins hosted dart_tui for the published
  # package — two different graphs; an audit of one says nothing about the
  # other. Each graph gets its own matrix leg and the split is documented in
  # the audit output.
  dep-audit:
    name: Dependency audit (${{ matrix.graph }})
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: changes
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        graph: [hosted, vendored]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      # Hosted leg = exactly what pub.dev consumers resolve; the overrides
      # file never ships, so it must not bend this graph.
      - name: Park vendored overrides (hosted leg)
        if: matrix.graph == 'hosted'
        run: |
          [ -f pubspec_overrides.yaml ] || {
            echo "::error::pubspec_overrides.yaml missing — hosted-leg precondition broke, parking nothing would bend the graph silently"
            exit 1
          }
          mv pubspec_overrides.yaml pubspec_overrides.yaml.vendored
      - run: dart pub get
      - name: Audit the ${{ matrix.graph }} dependency graph
        env:
          GRAPH: ${{ matrix.graph }}
        run: |
          {
            echo "### Dependency audit — \`${GRAPH}\` graph"
            echo ""
            echo "This repo resolves TWO dependency graphs (SEC-08):"
            echo "- **hosted** — \`pubspec.yaml\` alone: what \`pub publish\` ships and pub.dev consumers resolve (dart_tui hosted)."
            echo "- **vendored** — \`pubspec.yaml\` + \`pubspec_overrides.yaml\`: local dev, CI and the release binaries (dart_tui rides \`vendor/dart_tui\`)."
            echo ""
            echo "An audit of one says nothing about the other, so both are audited on every run. Resolved graph:"
            echo ""
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          dart pub deps --style=compact | tee /tmp/graph.txt >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY" || true
          {
            echo ""
            echo "Outdated direct dependencies (informational):"
            echo '```'
            dart pub outdated
            echo '```'
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY" || true
          # The split must be REAL: each leg resolves dart_tui from its own
          # source, read from the resolved pubspec.lock. The block runs from
          # the `dart_tui:` entry header to the next top-level entry header
          # (two-space indent) — no fixed line window to rot.
          lock_block=$(awk 'f && /^  [A-Za-z0-9_.-]+:$/ { exit } /^  dart_tui:$/ { f = 1 } f { print }' pubspec.lock)
          # Vacuous-assertion guard: if dart_tui ever leaves the lock (or
          # the entry is renamed) the block is empty and the per-graph
          # greps below would fail bare (exit 1, no annotation) or — worse
          # for future shape changes — pass on nothing. Fail loudly here.
          [ -n "$lock_block" ] || {
            echo "::error::no dart_tui entry found in pubspec.lock — the audit assertion is vacuous, aborting"
            exit 1
          }
          echo "$lock_block"
          case "$GRAPH" in
            hosted)
              if echo "$lock_block" | grep -q 'source: path'; then
                echo "::error::hosted graph resolved the vendored dart_tui fork"
                exit 1

#!/usr/bin/env bash

blocks.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# check_action_pins.sh — SEC-08 (#796) AC1/AC4: mutable references to
# executable code are lint errors. Fails on any third-party GitHub Actions
# `uses:` ref that is not pinned to a full commit SHA.
#
#   bash scripts/check_action_pins.sh            # scan the repo (CI gate)
#   bash scripts/check_action_pins.sh --path DIR # scan DIR/*.yml (fixtures)
#
# Exempt:
#   - ./...          first-party repo-relative actions/workflows
#   - @<40-hex>      full commit SHA (the only accepted third-party form)
# Everything else (tags, branches, latest, main, master, short SHAs) fails.

set -eu

dir=".github/workflows"
if [ "${1:-}" = "--path" ]; then
  [ -n "${2:-}" ] || { echo "usage: $0 [--path DIR]" >&2; exit 2; }
  dir="$2"
fi

shopt -s nullglob
# Both modes share one shape: the root's workflows (either a
# .github/workflows layout or loose *.yml/*.yaml fixtures) plus EVERY
# composite action manifest at any depth — composite action steps can
# carry remote uses: refs, so they are part of AC1's threat surface.
files=("$dir"/.github/workflows/*.yml "$dir"/.github/workflows/*.yaml \
       "$dir"/*.yml "$dir"/*.yaml)
# Default (CI) mode: composite actions live under .github/actions/, OUTSIDE
# the workflows dir — root the manifest sweep at the repo root so they
# are covered (a regression here would let an unpinned remote uses: sail
# through AC1). Prune .worktrees: sibling checkouts are not this repo's
# gate surface. Fixture mode (--path) stays rooted at DIR: fixtures are
# self-contained trees.
root="$dir"
if [ "$dir" = ".github/workflows" ] && [ -d "$dir" ]; then
  root="."
fi
while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
  files+=("$f")
done < <(find "$root" -name .git -prune -o -path './.worktrees' -prune -o -type f \( -name 'action.yml' -o -name 'action.yaml' \) -print0 2>/dev/null)

if [ ${#files[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "no workflow files found under $dir" >&2
  exit 2
fi

violations=0
for file in "${files[@]}"; do
  refs=$(grep -hoE '^[[:space:]]*(-[[:space:]]+)?uses:[[:space:]]*[^[:space:]]+' "$file" 2>/dev/null | sed -E 's/.*uses:[[:space:]]*//') || true
  [ -n "$refs" ] || continue
  while IFS= read -r ref; do
    [ -n "$ref" ] || continue
    case "$ref" in
      ./*) ;; # first-party repo-relative action/workflow
      docker://*)
        case "$ref" in
          *@sha256:*) ;; # digest-pinned container image
          *)
            echo "::error file=$file::unpinned container image ref: $ref"
            violations=$((violations + 1))
            ;;
        esac
        ;;
      *)
        sha="${ref##*@}"
        # A mutable ref whose NAME is exactly 40 chars would pass a pure
        # length glob — require hex digits (a commit SHA), nothing else.
        if [[ "$sha" =~ ^[0-9a-fA-F]{40}$ ]]; then
          : # full 40-hex commit SHA — the only accepted third-party form
        else
          echo "::error file=$file::third-party action not SHA-pinned: $ref"
          violations=$((violations + 1))
        fi
        ;;
    esac
  done <<EOF
$refs
EOF
done

if [ "$violations" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo "check_action_pins: $violations mutable third-party action ref(s)" >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "check_action_pins: OK (all third-party actions SHA-pinned)"

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger …

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1222
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1222
- **Title**: chore(pin): awf workflows track @main — always-latest policy (kicker fixes live on merge)
- **Author**: IstiN
- **Branch**: `pin/awf-kicker-fd84ab19` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +27
- **Deletions**: -22
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T07:00:24Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T15:19:18Z

## PR Description

Owner directive 2026-10-04: consumers follow awf main instead of immutable SHA pins — fixes (kicker real ticks awf#13, per-SHA concurrency awf#14, teammate defaults awf#12) go live on merge, no re-pin ceremony per consumer.

Security trade-off (accepted by owner): a mutable ref executes whatever sits at awf main head. Mitigation: awf main is load-bearing — review-gated pushes only; stub-ref guard tests assert every awf uses: is exactly main (never a stale SHA, never a random ref); the agents submodule gitlink stays an immutable ENGINE pin via factory_ref.

Supersedes the original fd84ab19 re-pin description (pre-directive plan).

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1222._

> ℹ️ **3 thread(s) already resolved and excluded from this review.**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 4 — `test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the rewritten guard still covers only 3 of the 5 awf callers this PR flips — the promised "every awf uses: is exactly main" invariant is enforced for teammate/SM/merge only**

Carried over from the previous round (unresolved in this diff). The guard rewrite itself is correct — `pinnedRef` now returns the literal ref and the tests assert `ref == 'main'` — but the caller map is unchanged:

```dart
// test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart (still 3 entries)
final stubs = <String, (String, String)>{
  'ai-teammate.yml': (teammate, 'factory-teammate.yml'),
  'machine-sm.yml':  (sm, 'factory-sm.yml'),
  'machine-merge.yml': (merge, 'factory-merge.yml'),
};
```

- `sm-kicker.yml` is read only by `test/machine_kit/sm_kicker_test.dart`, which asserts the `uses:` line merely *starts with* `factory-sm-kicker.yml@` — **any** ref (`@main`, a stale SHA, a random branch) passes. Nothing pins it to `main`.
- `merge-trigger.yml` is read by no test at all — its ref is entirely unguarded, and it is the highest-privilege leg (`workflow_run`-triggered, `contents: write`, `secrets: inherit` executing whatever sits at awf main).

Both legs are currently at `@main` (verified), so nothing is broken today — this is enforcement debt, not a red CI. But the map's own doc comment says "New stubs MUST be added here … an unlisted stub escapes all three [checks]", and the PR description's stated mitigation claims coverage of *every* awf `uses:`. The exact regression class the policy now needs to catch — "one leg re-pinned to a stale SHA or a random ref while the rest track main" — is precisely the one these two legs escape.

Please add `sm-kicker.yml` → `factory-sm-kicker.yml` and `merge-trigger.yml` → `factory-merge-trigger.yml` to the map (making it 5 entries), and settle the pre-existing inconsistency while there: `merge-trigger.yml` delegates with `secrets: inherit`, while the guard's secrets test enforces explicit `SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN` mapping on the other three stubs (the factory's required-secret validation rejects `inherit` at call time on those legs).

---

### Thread 5 — `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the pin comment directly above the new `@main` ref still argues the immutable-SHA policy — it now documents the opposite of the code**

Carried over from the previous round (unresolved in this diff — the comment block itself was not touched):

```yaml
# Pinned to an immutable SHA of IstiN/dmtools-agents (branch heads move;
# a branch ref executes whatever is at the head at run start). Flip in
# lockstep with the machine-sm.yml pin — guarded by
# test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml@main
```

Three problems after the flip:

1. **The rationale is inverted**: "a branch ref executes whatever is at the head at run start" is framed as a hazard to avoid, but executing awf main at run start is now the *policy* (owner directive 2026-10-04, review-gated always-latest). A future reader following this comment would "fix" `@main` back to a SHA and silently freeze the loop off awf fixes — exactly the regression the rewritten guard exists to catch.
2. **Wrong repo**: the comment says "immutable SHA of IstiN/dmtools-agents", but the callee here is `IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows` (dmtools-agents is the ENGINE, pinned separately via `factory_ref:`, which correctly stays a SHA).
3. **"Pinned" is no longer accurate** — this tracks a moving head by design; the correct verb is "tracks".

Please rewrite the block to state the always-`main` policy (owner directive 2026-10-04; awf main is load-bearing / review-gated as the accepted trade-off; the ENGINE stays pinned via `factory_ref`) and keep the guard citation — that part is accurate again now that `factory_stub_ref_test.dart` asserts `@main`.

The same stale framing sits in `machine-sm.yml:51`: "Pinned to the immutable dmtools-agents main @f59104948fec3e8dc5fe5b26fa92e538f73a5019 — ships: …" (that line is outside this diff's hunks, but it describes the exact line this PR changes at `machine-sm.yml:72` and deserves the same rewrite).

---

### Thread 6

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

    if: needs.gate.result == 'success' && (needs.gate.outputs.issue != '' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch')
    # Job-scoped grants mirroring the pinned callee's declared scopes (a
    # reusable call is capped by the calling job's effective permissions —
    # see the top-level comment). Scoped to THIS job so any future job in
    # this workflow defaults to the top-level read-only.
    permissions:
      contents: write         # the factory pushes branches / session trees
      issues: write           # labels, comments, close-issue safety net
      pull-requests: write    # PR creation, review threads, update-branch
      actions: write          # actions/cache save phase + workflow_dispatch
    # Pinned to an immutable SHA of IstiN/dmtools-agents (branch heads move;
    # a branch ref executes whatever is at the head at run start). Flip in
    # lockstep with the machine-sm.yml pin — guarded by
    # test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml@main
    with:
      # The literal uses-ref: the factory requires it (it cannot derive its
      # own ref — github.workflow_ref in a called workflow is the CALLER's).
      factory_ref: e166ef7774822fabd39bebe7b950074be6892731
      flutter-version: 'stable'  # explicit: awf no longer defaults to a Flutter toolchain
      # STRING — number/choice-typed reusable inputs cannot take expressions.
      issue: ${{ needs.gate.outputs.issue || github.event.inputs.issue }}
      # #687: PR-anchored review (SM dispatches with pr instead of issue).
      pr: ${{ github.event.inputs.pr || '' }}
      # #687: machine login via jobParams — branch-independent (the
      # checked-out PR branch carries no machineAuthor config).
      machine-author: ${{ vars.MACHINE_AUTHOR || '' }}
      leg: ${{ needs.gate.outputs.leg || github.event.inputs.leg || '' }}
      reason: ${{ github.event.inputs.reason || 'ai-teammate-author gate' }}

    secrets:

blocks.text:
# Factory Merge Trigger — the canonical pr_approved merge bot.
#
# One reusable implementation for every factory repo. The calling repo
# keeps a thin stub that declares the EVENT triggers (workflow_run on its
# CI workflow, optionally issues:labeled) and calls this one — `on:` in a
# stub cannot be parameterized, everything below the event boundary is
# shared here.
#
# The tracker is the CALLING repo's GitHub issues (no Jira, no external
# services):
#
#   issue labeled `pr_approved` → linked PR found → required checks green
#   (branch protection is the gate: mergeStateStatus CLEAN) → squash-merge
#   → label removed → comment posted on the issue.
#
# Linking conventions (any of):
#   - PR body contains `Closes #NN` / `Fixes #NN` / `Resolves #NN`
#   - PR branch name starts with `NN-` (e.g. `42-fix-foo`)
#   - PR branch name matches `gh-0*NN` (the gh-N display-title convention)
#   - the PR itself carries the label (pr_review approves via
#     scm.addLabel) — mapped back to its linked issue
#
# Prerequisites (in the calling repo):
#   vars: MERGE_TRIGGER_ENABLED (fuse — the job skips itself until `true`)
#   branch protection on main with required checks + strict (the machine
#   only merges CLEAN PRs, so protection defines what "ready" means).
#   github.token is sufficient for everything; pass a PAT via
#   secrets: inherit if the caller needs one (see GH_TOKEN below).

name: Factory Merge Trigger

run-name: 'Merge Trigger : CI passed → merge pr_approved issues'

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      runner:
        description: 'Runs-on label for the merge job'
        type: string
        default: 'ubuntu-latest'
      remove_pr_label:
        description: 'Also remove pr_approved from the merged PR (dmd convention)'
        type: boolean
        default: true
      map_pr_labels:
        description: 'Map PRs labeled pr_approved back to their linked issues'
        type: boolean
        default: true
      gh_branch_pattern:
        description: 'Also link via branch names like gh-0*NN'
        type: boolean
        default: true

permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write
  actions: read

jobs:
  merge-trigger:
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner }}
    timeout-minutes: 10
    # Same-repo guard: PRs from forks must not trigger merges. The
    # issues:labeled entry path (dmd) re-enters without a workflow_run.
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'issues' && github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved') ||
      (github.event_name == 'workflow_run' &&
       github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success' &&
       github.event.workflow_run.head_repository.full_name == github.repository)
    concurrency:
      group: merge-trigger-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha || github.event.issue.number }}
      cancel-in-progress: false
    steps:
      - name: Gate on MERGE_TRIGGER_ENABLED
        id: gate
        env:
          ENABLED: ${{ vars.MERGE_TRIGGER_ENABLED }}
        run: |
          if [ "$ENABLED" = "true" ]; then
            echo "enabled=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "enabled=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::merge-trigger scaffold is wired but disabled — set the MERGE_TRIGGER_ENABLED repo variable to true (after branch protection + required checks are in place)."
          fi

      - name: Merge issues labeled pr_approved
        if: steps.gate.outputs.enabled == 'true'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.PAT_TOKEN || github.token }}
          LABEL: pr_approved
          CI_RUN_URL: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.html_url }}
          REMOVE_PR_LABEL: ${{ inputs.remove_pr_label }}
          MAP_PR_LABELS: ${{ inputs.map_pr_labels }}
          GH_BRANCH_PATTERN: ${{ inputs.gh_branch_pattern }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          repo="${{ github.repository }}"
          # Candidates come from BOTH sides: the issue label (human/bot)
          # and the PR label (pr_review approves via scm.addLabel on the
          # PR) — map PR labels back to their linked issues.
          issues=$(gh issue list --repo "$repo" --label "$LABEL" --state open \
            --json number --jq '.[].number')
          if [ "$MAP_PR_LABELS" = "true" ]; then
            prs_labeled=$(gh pr list --repo "$repo" --label "$LABEL" --state open \
              --json number,body,headRefName --jq '.[] | "\(.number)\t\(.body // "")\t\(.headRefName)"')
            while IFS=$'\t' read -r prn body branch; do
              [ -n "$prn" ] || continue
              n=$(echo "$body" | grep -oiE '\b(closes|fixes|resolves)\s+#[0-9]+' | head -1 | grep -oE '[0-9]+' || true)
              [ -n "$n" ] || n=$(echo "$branch" | grep -oE '^[0-9]+' || true)
              [ -n "$n" ] || n=$(echo "$branch" | grep -oE 'gh-[0-9]+' | head -1 | grep -oE '[0-9]+' || true)
              if [ -n "$n" ]; then
                open=$(gh issue view "$n" --repo "$repo" --json state --jq .state 2>/dev/null || true)
                [ "$open" = "OPEN" ] && issues="$issues $n"
              fi
            done < <(printf '%s\n' "$prs_labeled")
            issues=$(echo $issues | tr ' ' '\n' | sort -u | tr '\n' ' ')
          fi
          if [ -z "${issues// /}" ]; then
            echo "no issues labeled '$LABEL' — nothing to merge"
            exit 0
          fi
          merged=0; skipped=0
          for n in $issues; do
            echo "::group::issue #$n"
            gh_pat='(?i)\\b(closes|fixes|resolves)\\s+#'"$n"'\\b'
            branch_pat='^'"$n"'[-_.]'
            if [ "$GH_BRANCH_PATTERN" = "true" ]; then
              link_sel="((.body // \"\") | test(\"$gh_pat\")) or (.headRefName | test(\"$branch_pat\")) or (.headRefName | test(\"(^|[-_./])gh-0*$n$\"))"
            else
              link_sel="((.body // \"\") | test(\"$gh_pat\")) or (.headRefName | test(\"$branch_pat\"))"
            fi
            pr=$(gh pr list --repo "$repo" --state open \
              --json number,body,headRefName \
              --jq "[.[] | select($link_sel) | .number] | first // empty")
            if [ -z "$pr" ]; then
              echo "issue #$n: no linked open PR (add 'Closes #$n' to the PR body or name the branch '$n-…') — skipping"
              skipped=$((skipped+1)); echo "::endgroup::"; continue
            fi
            state=$(gh pr view "$pr" --repo "$repo" \
              --json mergeable,mergeStateStatus \
              --jq '.mergeable + ":" + .mergeStateStatus')
            echo "linked PR #$pr — $state"
            case "$state" in
              MERGEABLE:CLEAN)
                if err=$(gh pr merge "$pr" --repo "$repo" --squash 2>&1); then
                  merged=$((merged+1))
                  gh issue edit "$n" --repo "$repo" --remove-label "$LABEL" || true
                  if [ "$REMOVE_PR_LABEL" = "true" ]; then
                    gh pr edit "$pr" --repo "$repo" --remove-label "$LABEL" || true
                  fi
                  gh issue comment "$n" --repo "$repo" \
                    --body "🔀 Merged #$pr (CI: ${CI_RUN_URL:-run})" || true
                  echo "✅ merged #$pr for issue #$n"
                else
                  skipped=$((skipped+1))
                  echo "❌ merge of #$pr failed: $err"
                fi
                ;;
              MERGEABLE:BEHIND)
                skipped=$((skipped+1)); echo "⏳ behind main — the SM (silent-update-behind) refreshes it, then re-dispatches CI"
                ;;
              MERGEABLE:BLOCKED|MERGEABLE:UNSTABLE)
                skipped=$((skipped+1)); echo "⏳ required checks not green yet"
                ;;
              *)
                skipped=$((skipped+1)); echo "⛔ not mergeable ($state) — needs manual attention"
                ;;
            esac
            echo "::endgroup::"
          done
          echo "summary: merged=$merged skipped=$skipped"

# SM kicker — a tiny watchdog (two jobs, seconds each, ~zero runner cost).
#
# Canonical home for the SM-kicker watchdog every factory repo points at.
# The calling repo keeps a thin stub workflow that calls this one with the
# repo-specific names (defaults match flutter_agent_harness).
#
# Why it exists: a repo whose CI is dispatch-only (no `on.push` on PR
# heads) and whose Machine SM is the sole trigger has two gaps that leave
# a PR BLOCKED forever with zero required-check contexts on its head:
#
#   1. SM dead: the cron tick missed/failed and nothing re-arms it.
#      Fix: if no SM run is queued/running/in-progress — dispatch one tick.
#
#   2. Head completeness: pushes WITHOUT code changes (pure main-merge
#      commits — the SM's own silent update-branch, or a manual
#      "merge main into branch") fire no workflows by design, yet strict
#      `up-to-date` protection demands FRESH required checks on the new
#      head SHA. Fix: if a PR head is a codeless merge commit (2 parents,
#      0 files vs first parent) and carries NEITHER of the required check
#      contexts NOR an active CI run — dispatch the CI workflow on it.
#
# Code-bearing pushes (dev/rework/WIP) are deliberately NOT touched here:
# their validation schedule stays owned by the SM ("intermediate pushes
# are free"). The schedule leg re-checks open PRs every 30 min to also
# cover bot pushes made with GITHUB_TOKEN (those fire no events at all).

name: Factory SM kicker

run-name: '🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}'

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      sm_workflow:
        description: 'File name of the Machine SM workflow in the caller repo'
        type: string
        default: 'machine-sm.yml'
      ci_workflow:
        description: 'File name of the validation CI workflow to dispatch'
        type: string
        default: 'ci.yml'
      ci_display_name:
        description: 'Workflow display NAME as it appears in the runs API'
        type: string
        default: 'CI'
      required_contexts:
        description: 'Comma-separated required check context names'
        type: string
        default: 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      sm_workflow:
        description: 'SM workflow file'
        type: string
        default: 'machine-sm.yml'
      ci_workflow:
        description: 'CI workflow file to dispatch'
        type: string
        default: 'ci.yml'
      ci_display_name:

# Machine merge bot stub — event-driven fast path (factory pack).
#
# The SM cron tick is best-effort (GitHub silently drops scheduled runs);
# this workflow reacts to EVENTS: CI conclusion, label changes, head
# pushes, check-run completions — and runs the deterministic mergeBot
# (factory-merge.yml) so approved green PRs merge within seconds.
# Idempotent against the SM: shared labels, first actor wins.
name: 'Machine Merge Bot'

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ['CI', 'Quality']   # per-repo: fa's dispatched CI is named 'CI'
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
    types: [labeled, synchronize, edited]
  check_run:
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch: {}

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write

concurrency:
  group: machine-merge-bot
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  merge:
    # Label events only matter for the machine latches; other PR events
    # (synchronize/edited) always run — cheap and idempotent.
    if: >-
      github.event_name != 'pull_request' ||
      github.event.action != 'labeled' ||
      contains(github.event.label.name, 'ai_') ||
      contains(github.event.label.name, 'pr_approved')
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-merge.yml@main
    with:
      ci_workflow: ci.yml
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}

  those heads. Workaround until the upstream fix: keep the branch head
  code-bearing. Live instance: run 37193754301 on head 1fe9b1232.
- fix(messaging): gh-1180 — `schedule_message` self-chains no longer die
  silently at the agent-chatter wake cap. The idle inbox-wake gate
  (`InboxWakePolicy`, shared by the CLI and the app hosts) now exempts a
  delivered scheduled self-reminder (`[scheduled] ` prefix, from == to)
  from the 10-consecutive-wake streak: a deliberate agent-chosen cadence
  (night watch, periodic sweep) wakes forever, while foreign
  agent-to-agent chatter stays capped (anti-storm REG) and user-kind
  mail always wakes. A 30s cadence floor bounds a zero-delay
  re-schedule spin (E5). Refused wakes are visible (`[mail] wake

  `<messagesRoot>/_scheduled/receipts.jsonl` (`ScheduledReceiptLog`):
  scheduled / delivered / delivery_failed / scan_failed /

# SEC-08 (#796): CI supply-chain gate. Runs on EVERY PR — no path gating,
  # a security gate you can dodge with a cunning diff is not a gate.
  supply-chain:
    name: Supply-chain gate
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: changes
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # Known limit: pull_request/dispatched runs execute THIS file and the
      # checker from the PR's own head — a PR can edit the gate in the same
      # diff. Backstops: reviewers see workflow edits, Dependabot PRs
      # re-verify on main, and the gate is re-enforced by any post-merge
      # scheduled run. A hard guarantee needs a separate workflow_call gate
      # pinned by SHA, invoked from a caller that never comes from the PR
      # (follow-up issue, not this PR).

      # AC1: zero mutable third-party action refs (script + CI job).
      - name: AC1 — all third-party actions SHA-pinned
        run: bash scripts/check_action_pins.sh

      # AC2: every workflow declares an explicit top-level permissions block.
      - name: AC2 — every workflow declares top-level permissions
        run: |
          status=0
          shopt -s nullglob
          for f in .github/workflows/*.yml .github/workflows/*.yaml; do
            [ -f "$f" ] || continue
            if ! grep -q '^permissions:' "$f"; then
              echo "::error file=$f::missing top-level permissions: block"
              status=1
            fi
          done
          exit $status

      # AC4 (REG): the checker must reject a @v4 fixture, a 40-char NON-hex
      # ref (mutable branch with a SHA-shaped name), and a nested composite
      # action manifest — and accept clean equivalents. A gate that cannot
      # fail is decoration.
      - name: AC4 — pin-checker fixture regression
        run: |
          tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
          trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT
          mkdir -p "$tmp/bad" "$tmp/bad-hex" "$tmp/bad-composite/.github/actions/probe/deep" "$tmp/good" "$tmp/good-composite/.github/actions/probe/deep" "$tmp/string-safe"
          printf 'jobs:\n  probe:\n    steps:\n      - uses: actions/checkout@v4\n' > "$tmp/bad/bad.yml"
          printf 'jobs:\n  probe:\n    steps:\n      - uses: actions/checkout@gggggggggggggggggggggggggggggggggggggggg\n' > "$tmp/bad-hex/bad.yml"
          printf 'name: probe\nruns:\n  using: composite\n  steps:\n    - uses: actions/checkout@v4\n' > "$tmp/bad-composite/.github/actions/probe/deep/action.yaml"
          printf 'jobs:\n  probe:\n    steps:\n      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v4\n' > "$tmp/good/good.yml"
          printf 'name: probe\nruns:\n  using: composite\n  steps:\n    - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v4\n' > "$tmp/good-composite/.github/actions/probe/deep/action.yaml"
          # String-safety: a uses-shaped string INSIDE a run: scalar is not a
          # step ref — the checker is line-anchored (^[[:space:]]*(- )?uses:)
          # and must not flag it. (Regression: a reviewer suspected the
          # fixture printf lines in this very workflow would trip AC1.)
          printf "jobs:\n  probe:\n    steps:\n      - name: write fixture\n        run: |\n          printf 'jobs:\\\\n  probe:\\\\n    steps:\\\\n      - uses: actions/checkout@v4\\\\n' > out.yml\n          bash scripts/check_action_pins.sh --path . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true\n" > "$tmp/string-safe/wf.yml"
          for bad in bad bad-hex bad-composite; do
            if bash scripts/check_action_pins.sh --path "$tmp/$bad" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              echo "::error::pin checker FAILED to flag the $bad fixture"
              exit 1
            fi
          done
          bash scripts/check_action_pins.sh --path "$tmp/good" >/dev/null
          bash scripts/check_action_pins.sh --path "$tmp/good-composite" >/dev/null
          bash scripts/check_action_pins.sh --path "$tmp/string-safe" >/dev/null
          echo "fixture regression OK: @v4 / 40-char non-hex / unpinned nested composite rejected; SHA-pinned accepted; uses-shaped run-scalar strings ignored"

  # SEC-08 (#796): audit BOTH dependency graphs. pubspec_overrides.yaml
  # redirects dart_tui to the vendored fork (vendor/dart_tui) for local/CI/
  # release builds while pubspec.yaml pins hosted dart_tui for the published
  # package — two different graphs; an audit of one says nothing about the
  # other. Each graph gets its own matrix leg and the split is documented in
  # the audit output.
  dep-audit:
    name: Dependency audit (${{ matrix.graph }})
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: changes
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        graph: [hosted, vendored]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      # Hosted leg = exactly what pub.dev consumers resolve; the overrides
      # file never ships, so it must not bend this graph.
      - name: Park vendored overrides (hosted leg)
        if: matrix.graph == 'hosted'
        run: |
          [ -f pubspec_overrides.yaml ] || {
            echo "::error::pubspec_overrides.yaml missing — hosted-leg precondition broke, parking nothing would bend the graph silently"
            exit 1
          }
          mv pubspec_overrides.yaml pubspec_overrides.yaml.vendored
      - run: dart pub get
      - name: Audit the ${{ matrix.graph }} dependency graph
        env:
          GRAPH: ${{ matrix.graph }}
        run: |
          {
            echo "### Dependency audit — \`${GRAPH}\` graph"
            echo ""
            echo "This repo resolves TWO dependency graphs (SEC-08):"
            echo "- **hosted** — \`pubspec.yaml\` alone: what \`pub publish\` ships and pub.dev consumers resolve (dart_tui hosted)."
            echo "- **vendored** — \`pubspec.yaml\` + \`pubspec_overrides.yaml\`: local dev, CI and the release binaries (dart_tui rides \`vendor/dart_tui\`)."
            echo ""
            echo "An audit of one says nothing about the other, so both are audited on every run. Resolved graph:"
            echo ""
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          dart pub deps --style=compact | tee /tmp/graph.txt >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY" || true
          {
            echo ""
            echo "Outdated direct dependencies (informational):"
            echo '```'
            dart pub outdated
            echo '```'
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY" || true
          # The split must be REAL: each leg resolves dart_tui from its own
          # source, read from the resolved pubspec.lock. The block runs from
          # the `dart_tui:` entry header to the next top-level entry header
          # (two-space indent) — no fixed line window to rot.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
